{{Quote|Everything was great until the scandal hit about Veruna's Foreign Affairs. Suddenly things got tense around the house. Dad blamed Amidala. You couldn't even mention her name without him exploding into a rage.|Ian Lago, recalling the scandal|<ref name="ASD" />}}
Around [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], a '''corruption scandal''' related to [[King/Legends|King]] [[Ars Veruna/Legends|Ars Veruna's]] conduct or handling of the Foreign Affairs of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] was made public. Veruna's [[Prime Councilor|Prime Counselor]] [[Kun Lago]] was also believed to be involved in the scandal, while the young [[Politics/Legends|politician]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] was seen as responsible for bringing public attention to the issue. King Veruna abdicated the throne shortly after the incident.

==History==
===Prelude===
===Crisis===
{{Quote|Where have you ''been'', Ian? Are you so wrapped up in yourself you don't know what's going on here? We are ''this close'' to losing ''everything''! Our home, our reputation... ''Everything''!|Kun Lago to his son, Ian|<ref name="ASD" />}}
Sometime around [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]],<ref name="date" /> a corruption scheme linked to [[King/Legends|King]] [[Ars Veruna/Legends|Ars Veruna's]] administration of the foreign [[Politics/Legends|policy]]<ref name="SON">''[[Secrets of Naboo]]''</ref> of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] was revealed to the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Nabooan]] electorate. [[Kun Lago]], [[Prime Councilor|Prime Counselor]] to the [[Royal House of Naboo/Legends|monarch]], blamed [[Princess of Theed]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] for the eruption of the crisis, which had a greatly negative impact on the popularity of the king. Lago's son [[Ian Lago|Ian]], in turn, believed that his father was also involved in the scandal.<ref name="ASD" /> Since corruption in Naboo elected leaders was virtually unheard of, the king's double agenda was successful and unknown by the populace at first.<ref name="SON" /> Veruna's disastrous foray into offworld politics was initially encouraged by [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].<ref name="TVD">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

In the wake of the disclosure of Ars Veruna's involvement in the scandal, a crisis erupted<ref name="ASD" /> and the king soon abdicated the throne,<ref name="NEGC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> ending his thirteen year rule.<ref name="CWSE">{{CSWECite|III|304|Veruna, King}}</ref> The popular Amidala, whose bid for the throne had initially been suggested to her parents, and subsequently discreetly backed by Palpatine,<ref name="DPN">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> was quickly elected and [[Coronation of Queen Amidala/Legends|crowned]] his successor as [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Monarch of Naboo]].<ref name="ASD" />

===Aftermath===
{{Quote|Stop passing the ''blame''! ''You screwed up'' and you got ''caught''! Now you're goin' down and you want to blame it on the only truly ''good'' person I've ever known!|Ian Lago arguing with his father|<ref name="ASD" />}}
While Kun Lago was dismissed of his post and his son Ian left the planet,<ref name="ASD" /> Veruna chose to flee [[Theed/Legends|Theed]],<ref name="DPN" /> the planetary seat of government.<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> The former king sought refuge in the [[Earl of Vis' castle|castle]] of the [[Earl of Vis/Legends|Earl of Vis]], located in the remote [[Western Reaches (Naboo)|Western Reaches]] of the planet, where soon afterwards he would be murdered by [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]].<ref name="DPN" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Kun_Lago_running_about.png|thumb|250px|Kun Lago (in purple) during the crisis]]
The Foreign Affairs scandal was introduced in the [[Star Wars Tales 5|fifth issue]] of ''[[Star Wars Tales]]'', in the short comic "[[A Summer's Dream]]." The comic was written by [[Terry Moore]] and published on [[September 27]], [[2000]] by [[Dark Horse Comics]]. In the story, the scandal is shown as an important reason why Kun Lago resents Padmé Amidala so strongly, and tries to oppose his son's relationship with the princess. The story hints that Amidala was behind the publicizing of the scandal, that Kun Lago was involved in it, and that the king's abdication was significantly influenced by this event.<ref name="ASD" />

Although stories from issues 1 to 20 of ''Star Wars Tales'' are usually considered to be ambiguously [[canon]],<ref name="Chee">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=752#14952461|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2006-06-04|time=3:05 AM}}</ref> the events described in ''A Summer's Dream'' were included in other canonical works, fitting the story into the overall ''[[Star Wars]]'' continuity. The foreign policy scandal was cited in the [[2002]] book ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' and vaguely mentioned in a few other reference books such as the [[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary|''Star Wars: Episode I The Visual Dictionary'']],<ref name="TVD" /> ''[[Secrets of Naboo]]'',<ref name="SON" /> and ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''.<ref name="CWSE" />
